clue.text: Project meeting initially held in Notts town

indicators.note: the first letter of held is placed in the town's name, signalling a container

parts.note: Worksop is a town in Nottinghamshire (Notts)

indicators.note: initially points to just the opening letter of the word held

explanation.surface: A planning get-together was first held in a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H, which goes 'in' WORKSOP, a market town in Nottinghamshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a session where a group meets to work through a project together.

clue.text: European turned up in French port shortly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
shortly means the port's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany, France

explanation.surface: A European traveller arrived in a French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims BREST to BRES, and 'turned up' reverses it to SERB in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Serb is a native of Serbia, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Pass the down clues prior to this?

definitions.text: Pass the down clues prior to this?

parts.words: Pass the down clues prior to this?
parts.note: the clues before this one in the down list are numbered 1 and 2, and a football pass returned at once is named after those numbers

explanation.surface: An instruction to skip the earlier down clues.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a one-two is a quick return pass between two players; the clue also points at down clues 1 and 2, which come before this clue, 3.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall pass in football, played and returned immediately, carries that numbered name.

clue.text: Chief river of Germany

definitions.meaning: chief as in principal or most important
the ... flows through Frankfurt to join the Rhine

explanation.surface: The most important waterway in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means principal, and it is also a major German river joining the Rhine at Mainz.

clue.text: Ostentatious fellow entertaining child in apartment

indicators.note: in places the fellow-and-child group inside the word for an apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the fellow holds the child inside him

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a boy is a child

explanation.surface: A showy man is hosting a youngster at his flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like amusing, but here it means hosting: the child sits inside the fellow, and that group goes 'in' the apartment just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant means showy and attention-seeking, the same as ostentatious.

clue.text: Soundly beats an economist

indicators.note: Soundly signals that the word for beats is said aloud, giving a name of the same sound

parts.note: canes means beats with a stick

explanation.surface: A thrashing for an economist, delivered thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly', but it signals a homophone: CANES said aloud matches the economist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: Dog chewed bream caught in river

indicators.note: caught in means the mixed-up fish is held inside the river's name

parts.note: the Don is a river in Russia and in England

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters of bream are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog gnawed a fish it had caught in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges BREAM to BERMA, which is 'caught in' DON, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dobermann is a large German breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Wild animal, say, from Kuala Lumpur?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of animal and say are thrown about

explanation.surface: A creature of the jungle, perhaps, from the Malaysian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the letters of ANIMAL and SAY; the question mark marks Kuala Lumpur as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia, so someone from there is a Malaysian.

clue.text: Out when general practitioner first appears

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

indicators.note: first appears means only the opening letter of practitioner shows

explanation.surface: Unconscious by the time the family doctor shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general practitioner' reads as a GP, but 'general' is LEE and 'first appears' takes P from practitioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is out, dead to the world.

clue.text: A bulk order is capital

indicators.note: order means arrange, so the letters of A bulk are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A large purchase is a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges the letters of A BULK.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabul is the capital city of Afghanistan.

clue.text: Shelter oriental people inside building

indicators.note: inside places the oriental people within the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
E for eastern, oriental
men are people

explanation.surface: Refuge for Eastern folk within a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelter' looks like a verb but is a noun here; 'oriental' gives E, the compass abbreviation for east, and 'inside' puts it with the people within the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into rented flats.

clue.text: Chef cut squash or more tasty salad ingredients

indicators.note: cut means the word chef is docked of its final letter
squash means crush, so the letters of or more tasty are reshaped

explanation.surface: A cook trims the squash, or some tastier things for a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of CHEF to give CHE; 'squash' looks like the vegetable but rearranges OR MORE TASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Small round red fruits are often tossed whole into salads.

clue.text: Showers start off discussions

indicators.note: start off means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: brainstorms are group discussions to generate ideas

explanation.surface: Rainy weather begins the debates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' removes the first letter of BRAINSTORMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy falls of rain are showers on a larger scale.

clue.text: Postgraduates brought in to change old university

indicators.note: brought in to means the postgraduates are put inside the word for change

parts.note: alter means change
an MA is a Master of Arts, a postgraduate degree
the plural gives a second MA

explanation.surface: Graduate students are recruited to reform a former college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Postgraduates' is plural, so it gives two MAs, 'brought in to' ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the Latin phrase for the institution you studied at.

clue.text: Man said to provide stimulus

indicators.note: said signals that the word for stimulus is spoken, matching the name

parts.note: a fillip is a boost or stimulus

explanation.surface: A fellow who is reported to give a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' marks a homophone: FILLIP sounds like the man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip is a male first name, so it stands for an example of a man.

clue.text: Teach naughty child a school subject

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
art is a subject taught at school

explanation.surface: Instruct a mischievous pupil in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge is to pass it on, as a teacher does.

clue.text: Going off after a short time, moving at a steady pace

indicators.note: after puts the going-off word behind the time letter

parts.note: T is short for time
food going off is rotting

explanation.surface: Spoiling a little later while jogging along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' is rotting, not leaving; it comes 'after' T, short for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse trotting goes at a brisk, even gait between walk and canter.

clue.text: First of dancers is ready for ballroom routine? That can't be true

indicators.note: First of picks only the opening letter of dancers

parts.note: in formation, ready for a formation dance, a team ballroom routine

explanation.surface: A dancer is set for a set-piece number, yet the story is false.
explanation.walkthrough: D, then IS, then IN FORMATION, lined up for a formation dance, a team routine in ballroom dancing. The definition describes false information.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately false information is a claim that cannot be true.

clue.text: Confounded union leader caught in the act

indicators.note: in puts the union leader and caught letters inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of union

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bewildered trade union boss is caught red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes U from union; U and C go 'in' DEED. 'Caught in the act' reads as one idiom but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuced is an old-fashioned intensifier like damned, the same as confounded.

clue.text: Snazzy limo with a name on: J R Ewing?

indicators.note: snazzy means flashy and jazzed up, so the letters of limo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stylish limousine with a name badge belonging to the Dallas tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snazzy' rearranges the car's letters, then A and N for name follow. J R Ewing is the oil baron in the American TV soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: J R Ewing ran an oil company in the series Dallas, an example of a petroleum tycoon.

clue.text: Class storming out during test

indicators.note: during means the mixed letters sit within the test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: storming means wild and violent, so the letters of out are tossed about

explanation.surface: A pupil storms out in the middle of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storming' rearranges OUT to UTO, placed 'during' TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching session, a class.

clue.text: Millionaire's island

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the rich man's word has the island within it

explanation.surface: A rich man's private island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has': MILLIONAIRE has the island in its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Card given back to traitor?

indicators.note: given back means the letters of to and the traitor word are read in reverse

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A playing card returned to a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given back' reverses TO and RAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot card is one of a deck used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Swindle involving rear admiral and politician

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A fraud implicating a senior naval officer and an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is British slang for a racket or con.

clue.text: Submissive types succeeded in Arabian republic

indicators.note: in places the succeeded letter inside the country

parts.note: Yemen is a republic on the Arabian peninsula
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Meek people prospered in an Arabian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S, the genealogy abbreviation for succeeded, inside YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men always agree with their boss, so they are compliant people.

clue.text: I'm overwhelmed by a friend's bitterness

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means I'm is engulfed by a and the friend word

parts.note: a crony is a close friend; the 's is a link meaning is
I'm gives IM with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: I'm swamped by a pal's resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' means engulfed, so I'm sits inside 'a friend'; the 's of friend's reads as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry ill feeling between people.
